_note: Wild nests (NPC colonies), docs/17-wild-nests.md; termite mounds, spider dens and aphid herds, docs/24-npcs.md. Level = highest level whose minPatchPoints <= the points of the strongest active player in the patch; never goes down. Times are hours at world speed 1 (divide by world speed).

pavement.name: Pavement Ants
pavement.style: Swarm: many Workers and Minor Soldiers. Acid Sprayers mow them down.

fire.name: Fire Ants
fire.style: Aggressive: few but strong Major Soldiers, Acid Sentries later. A swarm of Minor Soldiers pulls the Majors down; keep your own Majors out of the acid.

carpenter.name: Carpenter Ants
carpenter.style: Fortress: walls and pit traps, few soldiers. The pits swallow small ants: bring Trap-jaw Ants to break the defenses, or Major Soldiers. The defenses rebuild.

honeypot.name: Honeypot Ants
honeypot._stockPct: Percent of the level's normal food store, per resource: honeypot ants hoard Nectar in living storage jars.
honeypot.style: Hoarders: a big Nectar store, guarded by Workers and Minor Soldiers. Light to beat; bring Workers to carry it home.

trapjaw.name: Trap-jaw Ants
trapjaw.style: Ambushers: no Workers, just a few heavily armed big-jawed soldiers behind pit traps. Swarm them with Minor Soldiers, and bring a few Trap-jaw Ants for the pits.

termite.name: Termites
termite._note: A termite mound (docs/24-npcs.md): a rich, heavily defended mid-game target on its own wild site. Its tier follows the area's strongest active player (minPoints), never drops. Regrows slowly and never raids.
termite.style: Armoured fortress: soft Termite Workers and armoured Termite Soldiers behind walls and pits, packed with chewed wood. The armour shrugs off small bites, so Minor Soldiers, Acid Sprayers and Trap-jaw Ants die in droves. Send heavy hitters (Major Soldiers, Slave-makers, Supermajors, Rhinoceros Beetles) and plenty of carriers. A few Bullet Ants or Assassin Bugs can't get through so many.

spider.name: Trapdoor Spider
spider._note: A boss (docs/24-npcs.md): a cluster of trapdoor-spider burrows and their young. Too strong for any one player: it only fights a supercolony's joint raid of at least minPlayers players (Marz, 5 Nov 2026), and it takes about 3 big armies (tier 1) or 4 (tier 2). Regrows over a week and never raids.
spider.style: A cluster of trapdoor-spider burrows, a giant spider under every silk lid and their young all round. Their fangs cut through any ant. No single colony can take them: only a supercolony's joint raid.

_area: Where wild things live (docs/24-npcs.md): every patch within `range` patches (same region) of a patch with players gets a wild nest and an aphid herd. Termite mounds sit in patches where patch % every == offset, spider dens likewise, each spawned once a player lives within its range. Sites are extra spots in the wilds that never take one of the 12 colony spots. Every patch within `range` also gets a windfall site (docs/25-windfalls.md).

herds._note: Aphid herds (docs/24-npcs.md). A herd makes Nectar only while a player's ants tend it. nectarPerHour by level, before the gathering multiplier in formulas.json (levels follow the area leader like wild nests: npc.levels[].minPatchPoints). Honeydew piles up in the herd (up to storeHours of production) and the tenders carry it home every deliverEveryHours. Left untended for wanderAfterHours, the herd wanders to another patch nearby. Hours at world speed 1.
herds.name: Aphid Herd
herds.style: Aphids on a stem, dripping honeydew. Tend them and they make Nectar for you; anyone can drive your tenders off and take over.

windfalls._note: Windfalls (docs/25-windfalls.md): contested food that drops on the patch's windfall site. Every site rolls a new one every everyHours (skipped while one is still there, or when no active player lives within announceRange patches). It lasts lastsHours, then rots. pile: food by level (levels follow the area leader like herds), times the kind's size, split by the kind's mix; not affected by the gathering multiplier. guardChance: how often wild ants get there first (guards by level). Ants that claim it fight whoever is there, then hold it and carry a load home every deliverEveryHours (as much as they can carry). Players with a colony within announceRange patches get a report when one drops. kinds[].eaters: the wild species that come for it (wildParties); lastsHours on a kind overrides lastsHours; carryPct: share of a holder's cargo it can strip per load (a beetle's shell); parties: how many wild parties it draws. Hours at world speed 1.
windfalls.name: Windfall

grasshopper.name: Dead grasshopper
grasshopper.text: A grasshopper dropped out of the grass and didn't get up. Every colony nearby can smell it.

fig.name: Fallen fig
fig.text: A ripe fig split open on the ground, sweet and sticky. It won't stay unclaimed for long.

branch.name: Leafy branch
branch.text: The wind snapped off a branch full of fresh leaves. A cutter's dream, if you can hold it.

lizard.name: Dead lizard
lizard.text: A dead lizard lies in the wilds: a mountain of Protein. Every colony around will march for it.

beetle.name: Dead beetle
beetle.text: A ground beetle died on its back in the wilds. Plenty of meat inside, but the shell makes it slow work to strip.

sugar.name: Sugar spill
sugar.text: Someone spilled something sweet. Pure Nectar, but the sun dries it fast: a few hours and it's gone.

picnic.name: Picnic crumbs
picnic.text: The giants left a picnic behind: crumbs of bread, meat and fruit as far as an ant can see. Every nest around is coming.

wildParties._note: Wild nests go out for windfalls (docs/25-windfalls.md#wild-ants-come-for-windfalls). When a windfall drops, a wild nest within range patches whose species eats it (kinds[].eaters; any = every wild nest but spiders) sends a party after delayHours, with chance (a kind with parties draws that many, always). After each one sets off, another may follow with repeatChance until it rots. A party is partyShare of each of the nest's units and walks at speedPct. Wild holders carry carryEach per ant home each delivery on top of their castes' cargo (termites carry nothing otherwise). Hours at world speed 1.

scents._note: What an unscouted wild scent hints at (docs/24-npcs.md).

nest.name: Wild scent
nest.text: It smells sharp, of wild ants. You can't tell which kind, how many, or what they store.

herd.name: Sweet scent
herd.text: It smells sweet, like honeydew. Something here could make Nectar.

mound.name: Woody scent
mound.text: It smells of chewed wood and damp earth. Something big was built here.

den.name: Danger scent
den.text: Silk threads on the ground and no ants anywhere near. Every scout's antennae say: careful.

raids._note: Raids by wild nests on players in their patch. Gentle: a fraction (partyShare) of the nest's soldiers (castes with attack >= soldierMinAttack; Workers stay home), slow so players see them coming. The party is worth at most maxPartyValuePctOfTargetPoints % of the target's points, counted in resources (formulas.json points.resourcesPerPoint).

tuning._note: The armies the balance checks use (npm run combat, shared/test/nests.test.ts): a fair army for a player whose area is at each wild-nest level, and for each termite mound tier. Spider dens only fight joint raids, so denArmies are joint armies: 3 bigArmy for tier 1, 4 for tier 2 (one bigArmy is a strong late solo army). A fair army should win at least 90% of the time with moderate losses; half of it should pay far more. Not used by the game itself.

swarm._note: Army-ant swarms (docs/20-swarms.md): each player colony is visited every 1.5 to 2.5 days (everyHours), with warningHours of notice. Each sighting rolls one of three sizes (sizes, chance in %), hidden until scouted. Each size is the biggest swarm that the colony, with what it has at home when the swarm is spotted, still beats at least minWinRate of the time and, if maxLossPct is set, loses at most maxLossPct % of its ants' worth (counting its ants lost plus the share of knocked-down defenses that wouldn't rebuild; a colony with no ants measures against that share of its defenses), on average over `trials` simulated battles. Size 0 is the smallest party (`smallest`); size n is n packs. A colony that beats a swarm keeps its prey: prey.pctOfWorth % of the swarm's worth, split by prey.mixPct, at least prey.minHours of the colony's own total production (and at least prey.min), and it may go over the storage cap like mission cargo. Hours are at world speed 1.
swarm.name: Army ant swarm

sizes.name: Foraging column
sizes.blurb: a column your soldiers should handle

sizes.name: War column
sizes.blurb: a hard fight that will cost you

scouting._note: Scouting the swarm (docs/20-swarms.md): each Scout sent slips up to the column and back on its own with basePct, plus perScentReadingPct per Scent Reading level and perMimicryPct per Chemical Mimicry level, up to maxPct. The report comes back if at least one does; the rest are eaten.
